title: The effect of concussion history on cognitive-motor integration in elite hockey players.

sections.label: AIM
sections.text: To observe the effects of concussion history on cognitive-motor integration in elite-level athletes.

sections.label: METHODS
sections.text: The study included 102 National Hockey League draft prospects (n = 51 concussion history [CH]; n = 51 no history [NC]). Participants completed two computer-based visuomotor tasks, one involved 'standard' visuomotor mapping and one involved 'nonstandard' mapping in which vision and action were decoupled.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: We observed a significant effect of group on reaction time (CH slower) and accuracy (CH worse), but a group by condition interaction only for reaction time (p < 0.05). There were no other deficits found. We discussed these findings in comparison to our previous work with non-elite athletes.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: Previously concussed elite-level athletes may have lingering neurological deficits that are not detected using standard clinical assessments.
